item.title: Margaritas Rimmed With Degreaser Burn 5 People at a North Carolina Chili’s
item.description:
Five people suffered chemical burns after drinking margaritas rimmed with a white granulated substance misidentified as sugar at a Chili’s Grill & Bar in Forest City, N.C., a health official said.

The people who fell ill on Wednesday were three customers and two staff members who appeared to have been burned largely on and around their mouths, Megan Rollins, a spokeswoman at Foothills Health District, said in an interview on Saturday.

She said they sustained the injuries after contact with a degreaser, which had been left in an unlabeled container near the bar.

The district, which is responsible for food safety, immediately dispatched environmental health specialists to investigate the restaurant, Jason Masters, the public health director at Foothills Health District, said in an email.

The Forest City Police Department could not be reached on Saturday. It was unclear whether it had opened an investigation.

A representative for Chili’s said in a statement that the restaurant chain “took immediate action to support those affected and avoid further injuries.”

The chemical, which was not identified by name or brand, was brought into the Chili’s early on Oct. 26 by a contractor who had been hired to power wash the building’s exterior, Ms. Rollins said. The contractor was not identified.

That worker then handed the product to a restaurant employee, who left it by the bar. It wasn’t clear why the contractor gave the employee the product, Ms. Rollins said.

On Wednesday, another employee, who was prepping the bar before lunch service, discovered the product and placed some of it in containers at the margarita station.

“It’s almost like a little tray where they put water, lime juice,” Ms. Rollins said of the station. “And then on the other side of the tray is a place to put salt or sugar.”

(Margaritas at Chili’s can be served with salt or sugar rimmers, according to the drinks menu on the company’s website.)

When the restaurant opened, three customers who ordered margaritas reported feeling an instant burn upon consuming them and raised concerns with restaurant employees.

Two workers sampled the substance and experienced the same symptoms.

All five went immediately to local urgent care centers, which alerted emergency management operations for Rutherford County, Ms. Rollins said.

The county’s emergency management agency on Saturday declined to comment, citing “privacy and confidentiality considerations.”

The Foothills Health District immediately closed the restaurant on Wednesday, temporarily suspending its permit, Ms. Rollins said.

It is unclear how severe the burns were.

“They had pretty instantaneous symptoms,” Ms. Rollins said, “so they didn’t ingest any more than they did.”

According to the Merck Manual, caustic substances can burn any tissue they touch when swallowed, from the lips and tongue to the esophagus and stomach. Industrial products, in particular, are more concentrated than ones found in homes, according to Merck, “and thus tend to be more damaging.”

Solid substances like a granulated degreaser, however, might only stick to the lips, which may limit damage, according to Merck.

On Thursday, the Chili’s restaurant reopened after complying with safety requirements.

“The establishment was instructed to wash, rinse and sanitize any and all surfaces that may have come into contact with the unknown chemical,” Mr. Masters said in an email.

An employee at the Chili’s in Forest City declined to comment, but the company representative said in the statement that it had “thoroughly investigated the circumstances and addressed the issues specific to this location.”

item.title: A Florida Election Chief Urges In-Person Voting Over ‘Serious’ Postal Delays
item.description:
The supervisor of elections in one of Florida’s most populous counties is urging voters there to cast ballots at early voting stations or to deliver their mail ballots in person, rather than relying on the U.S. Postal Service, because of what he called “serious” delays with mail ballot delivery.

Joe Scott, the elections supervisor in Broward County, Fla., said his office had received dozens of reports from voters in recent weeks complaining that their completed ballots weren’t being delivered to his office in a timely manner. That process, Mr. Scott said, should take “two days tops,” but some voters told his office that it was taking over two weeks.

Voters generally cannot track their ballots in the mail, Mr. Scott said, but his office notifies voters when it receives their ballots. For ballots to be counted in Florida, they must be received by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

“People are asking, ‘Why is it taking so long for my ballot to get back?’” Mr. Scott said in a phone interview on Saturday. “At this point, even if the mail was running normal — which it’s not — it’s way too late to put your ballot in the mail.”

Mr. Scott added that the problem was likely more serious than what voters have told his office. “For every person that’s saying this,” Mr. Scott said, “there are 50 or 100 who aren’t.”

Mr. Scott, an elected Democrat, said he started growing concerned about the Postal Service’s handling of mail ballots in Broward County late last month, when the bulk of mail ballots were sent out to voters there who requested them. The county, home to about 1.1 million active voters, is often a swing county in Florida — including, famously, during the 2000 presidential election.

“I started getting calls from community leaders saying everyone got ballots except people in Hallandale Beach,” Mr. Scott said, referring to a city in southern Broward County that has more than 25,000 eligible voters. “When I looked it up, they were right.”

Mr. Scott said that he then alerted a Postal Service liaison, who said the agency would look into the problem, but that nothing more came of it. He said a vast majority of mail ballots for the city were subject to significant delivery delays.

“The Postal Service is dramatically degraded from what it used to be,” Mr. Scott said. “It is different. It is worse.”

The Postal Service did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Trump Calls Former Lawyer’s $50 Million Deal ‘Obnoxious and Outrageous’
item.description:
President Trump on Saturday strongly criticized his former lawyer, Alina Habba Mildon, saying it was “totally obnoxious and outrageous” for her to enter into a $50 million deal for work with a billionaire Venezuelan family seeking a pardon from the president.

Mrs. Mildon, while working as a senior adviser at the Justice Department, signed on last year as an extraordinarily well-compensated general counsel for a company started by the daughter of Julio Herrera Velutini, who was granted the pardon by Mr. Trump weeks later.

At a Halloween party on Saturday at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Fla., Mr. Trump tore into Mrs. Mildon when asked about the contract, calling it “not acceptable.”

“I thought it was terrible,” he told reporters. “I told her, and I said, ‘I don’t want her paid.’ I thought we had somebody speak to the people that did it, and she used her relationship to do that. And it was far too much.”

Mrs. Mildon, who served as a personal lawyer to Mr. Trump and then briefly as the U.S. attorney in New Jersey, signed a four-year contract to represent the family. It is unclear if the deal can be terminated early.

When Mr. Trump first learned about Mrs. Mildon’s arrangement from an article in The New York Times, he erupted and told aides and allies that Mrs. Mildon should donate a portion of the money to his future presidential library or another Trump-related entity.

Mr. Trump said Saturday that he did not necessarily expect Mrs. Mildon to make a donation to the library, but suggested that someone should.

“I expect maybe the people,” he said of the Herrera family. “I don’t know if anybody wants to make it. But it’s unacceptable what she did.”

The contract calls for the Herrera family to pay Mrs. Mildon $10 million a year for four years, along with a variety of bonuses. In total, she was guaranteed more than $50 million, according to interviews and documents obtained by The Times.

Mrs. Mildon formally began her work for the family on Jan. 1. Weeks later, Mr. Trump granted Mr. Herrera a full and unconditional pardon for a misdemeanor campaign finance violation. Mr. Herrera had faced felony bribery charges but struck an unusually lenient plea deal in 2025. Mrs. Mildon previously said she played no role in Mr. Herrera’s pardon.

She did not respond to a request for comment about Mr. Trump’s criticism on Saturday.

item.title: Long Beach Shuts Down Its Coastal Waters After Sewage Spill
item.description:
In August, two jet skiers became stranded after passing the breakwater, fighting to stay alive for hours.

In October, relentless waves from Post-Tropical Storm Rachel slammed into homes on the beachfront, with some houses becoming close to collapsing into the surf.

And on Saturday, 15 beaches had to be closed after a pipe burst and dumped nearly 30,000 gallons of sewage, with almost half of it spilling into the ocean.

Long Beach, Calif., can’t seem to catch a break.

The coastal city temporarily closed all of its open coastal swimming sites, including its bay swimming areas and lagoons, after a sewage spill that began Friday evening, the city said in a statement Saturday.

Precautionary closure of the city’s open coastal swimming areas will remain in effect until recreational water quality is assessed and meets state standards. The city has more than six miles of public beach.

Water sampling will begin Monday, the city said. It’s unclear when the closures will be lifted.

Local officials said contractors were working to help clean up the spill and repair the broken pipe.

In recent years, Long Beach has also had to regularly grapple with upstream sewage spills that have forced beach closures.

Long Beach sits downstream from much of Los Angeles County, and many of the spills do not originate from the city itself.

item.title: ‘I Came as Donald Trump’: The President Hosts a Luxury Halloween at Mar-a-Lago
item.description:
There were cheetah and zebra stripes on the walls and tables. Women wore sequined leotards and elaborate headdresses, and one couple flocked around in bright-feathered costumes of jungle birds. Then President Trump arrived.

“I came as Donald Trump,” he said, outfitted in his standard red tie and navy suit. “I didn’t have time to get — people spent a lot of time and money. Rich people. They spent nine hours getting ready. I had 10 minutes, so I came as Donald Trump.”

Such was the scene Saturday night, when hundreds gathered in the ballroom at Mar-a-Lago to celebrate Halloween with the president. The theme was the jungle, if an opulent one.

There was Alaskan king crab and a caviar bar. There were bongo drums and puppets. Attendees posted photos on social media that showed a pen at the club with a zebra and a miniature pony. Nothing too scary.

Much more frightening for Republicans is the political environment across the country. And yet even as they brace for potential losses on Tuesday, Mr. Trump, whose approval rating is near historic lows, was thrilled to be entertaining.

“Look at all my rich members,” he told reporters. “They spent all day getting ready. Look at these guys.”

He added: “These are the biggest guys on Wall Street.”

It was a striking tone, with polls showing voters souring even more on Mr. Trump’s handling of the economy. One recent one from The New York Times and Siena University found that a majority of voters blame Mr. Trump for the decline: 69 percent disapprove of his handling of the cost of living, 65 percent disapprove of the war in Iran, and nearly 75 percent disapprove of the high price of gas and diesel.

But for Mr. Trump, Mar-a-Lago is always a stage for his brand of gilded festivity.

There was Speaker Mike Johnson and Sergio Gor, the U.S. ambassador to India, in the cordoned-off section of the ballroom. Attorney General Todd Blanche, who traveled with Mr. Trump on Air Force One on Friday, told reporters that he planned to wear an astronaut suit to the party. Vice President JD Vance was back in Washington, dressed as Albus Dumbledore as part of a family Harry Potter set of costumes.

Mr. Trump entered the ballroom to fanfare and gabbed with reporters on the dance floor before mingling with his “rich friends,” as he kept calling them. He castigated Alina Habba Mildon, his former personal lawyer, over a $50 million deal she secured for work with a billionaire Venezuelan family seeking a pardon from the president. He weighed in on the feud between Representative Haley Stevens of Michigan and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for Senate.

And he addressed, for the first time, a report in The New York Times that Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia and an adviser to Mr. Trump, was the target of a Chinese spy plot.

“I have a lot of respect for him. I like him. We hope everything’s OK,” he said. “We’ll check it out. We’re going to check it out very closely.”

When asked if Mr. Huang would stay on as a member of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, Mr. Trump said he “would like to say yes.”

“I mean, unless we find out something to the contrary,” he said. “I’ve always found Jensen Huang to be very above board. But you know, you’re dealing in a very complex issue, I will say.”

The Halloween party landed at a complicated moment for the president. He has spent much of the last month crisscrossing the country holding rallies for Republican candidates, many of them even or lagging in the polls. Some have sought to distance themselves from the president’s unpopular policies.

Mr. Trump was originally scheduled to travel to Kansas on Saturday for a rally, then to Iowa on Sunday. But on Thursday, both were canceled. A day later, after the president chewed out a reporter for asking why the first rally was canceled, the events were back on, but rescheduled as a double-header on Sunday.

Before the Halloween bash, Mr. Trump spent much of the day at his golf course in West Palm Beach, and participating in virtual rallies for Republican candidates.

“I feel very good,” the president told reporters, with the feathered guests gawking at him. “I mean, I feel like we’re doing well. The country has never done better.”
